brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Keyboard-as-instrument metaphor is genuinely fresh, mapping letter keys to chromatic hues like piano keys to notes
Harmony mode buttons (Monochromatic/Triadic/Tetradic) cleanly translate music theory chords into color theory relationships
Bottom keyboard-shortcut legend reinforces the instrument framing with native-feeling kbd tags
dominant_weaknesses: Visual language is generic dark-dashboard; nothing in typography or layout evokes a musical instrument beyond the literal label
Hex code chips sit awkwardly inside swatches with heavy dark backgrounds, fighting the color they're meant to display
Static screenshot suggests no waveform, sustain, or audio-visual feedback — the 'play' promise is unfulfilled visually
fix_priorities: Add visible motion/audio feedback: ripples, sustain glows, or chord-stacking animation when keys are pressed
Redesign harmony cards so hex labels float or overlay subtly rather than sitting in opaque dark pills
Differentiate typography — a more expressive display face for 'Chromatic' and harmony names to match the instrument concept
Tighten spatial rhythm: the left panel has a huge empty void below the harmony buttons that breaks the composition
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral logic is strongest, visceral appeal is moderate via the rainbow keyboard, but reflective resonance with the musical-instrument metaphor stays surface-level.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits — the keyboard and harmony-chord mapping nail the concept structurally, but without motion, sound cues, or sustain visuals it reads as a color tool wearing a music costume.
